pillar_reactions.evidence: He had already picked the modality for the right reason before the call and said so in his opening answer: 'I noticed he does that a lot in his videos. He uses like multiple functional movements that help with that aspect. So that way you're not really hurt.' Asked whether the approach would work for him he answered 'Yeah. Yeah, I definitely do.' The strongest reaction came when commitment was tested: 'what he does is just, to me, it makes sense... I want to actually feel, like, have mobility. I'm tired of feeling stiff. I'm tired of being injured. So I want to try something different on this next time go around.'

Agreed with the framework and then asked for mechanics on the one thing he knows he cannot do — snacking: 'just can you give me an example of what would be like a protein that you would mix with like a snack?' The rep answered with Greek yogurt and a label caveat, which the prospect accepted. He had already volunteered his own failure mode without prompting — 'I do eat a lot of potato chips... at the office, they have like bowls of candy... I don't have like self-control' — and the eight-hour window was presented as a gradual ramp from twelve to ten to eight, which he did not push back on.

The pillar he responded to most concretely, and he described the mechanism back rather than just agreeing: 'I like the fact that there's accountability. Just because for me, I like the fact that I can have someone to lean on whenever I have questions. And just someone to help kind of push me. Like you said, he's going to help track me every week, which I like. So he can kind of tailor it to like, okay, you did good this week, I feel like you can do it a little bit harder next week, or okay, we did a little too hard this week, we can dial it back. I like the fact that you can kind of tailor it.' He had also volunteered earlier that responsiveness was already part of the appeal: 'I've heard he said that he's very responsive in the community.'

anchors.raw: No, not really. I have one, but it's like, it's only like a $300 limit a month. Or not a month, just a $300 limit.
anchors.note: The decisive fact of the call and it surfaced with one question. A single card with a $300 total limit alongside a $300 monthly surplus makes every structure on offer arithmetically impossible before it is proposed, and four of them were proposed anyway. The playbook's entire money play assumes revolving credit exists; here there is effectively none.

anchors.raw: To be honest with you, I wouldn't be able to because I got to pay my tuition. It's like $2,100 and I have to pay that in August.
anchors.note: He is already buying a large, dated, career-changing investment out of pocket — the Navy Sealift Command certification — and it competes directly for the same money. He raised it as the reason the 50/50 split failed. Worth noting as a pattern: he is not price-averse, he is fully allocated, and he has already demonstrated willingness to pay for a programme that changes his life.

anchors.raw: It says it's unable. It says we're sorry we're unable to offer a payment plan at this time.
anchors.note: An external underwriter's verdict on the prospect's capacity, delivered live and then repeated on a second device after the link was re-sent by email. This is the hardest affordability signal in the corpus — not a prospect's opinion of what he can afford but a lender's. The rep read it as a technical fault and kept going.

anchors.raw: it's been something that I've been following Trevor for, I think, a month now.
anchors.competitor: Trevor's free social content, plus his existing gym
anchors.note: Third occurrence of this pattern in the batch. He has been consuming the coach's free content for a month and has been back in a gym for three weeks at no marginal cost. Nothing in the presentation quantified what $6,000 adds beyond form correction and check-ins, and the free alternative was never contested.

anchors.raw: So I usually have, at the end of the month, like, leftover, what I put away is like $300.
anchors.competitor: Primal University at $199/month (not mentioned on this call)
anchors.note: Recorded as an anchor because it is the number that should have routed the conversation. A $300 monthly surplus sits directly above the $199/month community product the same rep offered another prospect the previous day, and the product was never named here. The anchor did not undercut the price so much as the price was never matched to the anchor.

unmet_demand.want: A price point reachable on roughly $300 a month with no credit available
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The lowest structure offered was about $1,200 a month, and the lowest total offered was $4,000. Primal University at $199 a month, cancel anytime, exists and was documented on another call in this same batch, and was never mentioned to him. This is a routing failure rather than a product gap in the catalogue — but from the prospect's side, nothing he could afford was ever put in front of him.

unmet_demand.want: A strength programme that will not re-injure a recurrent shoulder problem that has never been diagnosed
unmet_demand.why_unmet: This is his entire reason for being on the call — 'I want to get a workout routine to where I can build longevity with strength training' after two years of monthly flare-ups. The offer's answer is remote video form correction, which addresses technique but assumes technique is the cause. Nobody knows whether it is, because it has never been imaged, and nobody suggested finding out. Whether the programme serves this want is genuinely unestablished, and the movements involved load the exact joint in question.

unmet_demand.want: Training that fits a 4am wake-up, a 5am start and a ten-hour shift
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Partially served — the rep said the schedule would be taken into account and the sessions are 30-40 minutes — but the specific problem, that he already trains straight after a ten-hour shift on seven hours of sleep and is reliant on energy drinks to function, was acknowledged rather than solved. Sleep and stimulant load are check-in metrics rather than programme scope.

unmet_demand.want: Getting back to bouldering and long trail rides
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Volunteered as the thing he misses most and dropped entirely. The rep engaged with it socially — 'maybe not rock climbing, but at least bouldering' — and never connected it to the programme or used it in the goals ladder. Kettlebell strength almost certainly supports it, and nobody said so.
